newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC says 1997 off to excellent start.
newsitem.headline: SBC says 1997 off to excellent start.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corporation (SBC) said earnings grew strongly in the first quarter of 1997 and net profit after tax and minorities was well ahead of expectations.
"The main contribution to these very good results came from SBC Warburg and SBC Private Banking but SBC Switzerland and SBC Brinson also made good progress," the bank said in a statement.
"Net profit after tax and minorities was well ahead of expectations," the statement said.

It said provisions for non-performing loans exceeded statistically expected risk costs but that the excess provisioning requirement was covered by a special provision set aside for this purpose in 1996.
As usual, SBC provided no numbers in its first quarter report but did break down its commentary by business area.
"Commission incomes and trading revenues benefited from buoyant financial markets," SBC said, adding equities business achieved a record result.
Brokerage posted the biggest growth in abolute terms among commission-based revenues.
SBC said asset management fees and income from investment funds and securities underwriting were also well ahead of year-ago figures.
Net interest income remained broadly stable as it had for several quarters.

"Personnel expenses were higher compared with first quarter 1996 primarily due to a rise in performance-related payments but also to a slight increase in headcount at SBC Private Banking and in the IT (information technology) sector," SBC said.
Other expenses were in line with the quarterly average for 1996.
"Overall, in comparison with the equivalent 1996 period, operating expenses increased at a significantly slower rate than operating income," SBC said.
Depreciation, amortisation and provisions were slightly lower than the first quarter a year ago.
Tax expenses were considerably higher based on higher earnings.
